claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me start with a few questions.

**First, could you please tell me the names and ages of the children you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Before I can assess your eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances a bit better.

**Can you tell me what Alex's current situation is? For example, is Alex in full-time education, training, or something else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently left school and signed up with the careers service to figure out what to do next. They're in that period where they're trying to work out their next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to gather a bit more information to properly assess your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently receiving any benefits, such as Universal Credit, Employment and Support Allowance, or Jobseeker's Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question:

**Are you the person who Alex lives with, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Before I make my final assessment, let me check the eligibility rules to ensure I'm applying them correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now make my assessment. Let me explain the key rules that apply to Alex's situation:

According to the rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if they're under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. 

Importantly, the rules state: **"You can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services."**

In Alex's case:
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex has recently left school
- Alex has registered with the careers service
- Alex lives with you

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension period for having registered with a government-sponsored careers service after leaving education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Summary of your eligibility:**

✓ **You can claim Child Benefit for Alex for up to 20 weeks** from the date Alex registered with the careers service. This is because:
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex has left school and registered with a government-sponsored careers service
- Alex lives with you
- Alex is not claiming benefits in their own name

**Important:** After the 20-week period ends, your eligibility will depend on Alex's circumstances at that time. For example:
- If Alex enters approved education or training, you can continue to claim
- If Alex enters paid work (24 hours or more per week), you would stop being eligible
- If Alex claims certain benefits, you would stop being eligible

I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to make your claim and confirm the exact end date of the 20-week period. You may also want to check in with them as the 20 weeks approaches to discuss what happens next based on Alex's situation at that time.
